sources.title: LAY'S Heartwork Microinfluencer Report - Heartwork Packs - 18.09.2020
sources.content:
LAY’S #HEARTWORK PACKS TO MICRO INFLUENCERS
1st July – 14th September 2020

THE BRIEF
Building on the connect formed with close to 1500 micro-influencers from the Smile campaign, LAY’S continued the trend by introducing LAY’S #Heartwork special packs to the extended LAY’S family securing reach, awareness, engagement and brand love.

Furthermore, the idea was to ensure every corner of India learnt of the LAY’S #Heartwork campaign through multiple social media posts that showered gratitude and drove donations for the unsung heroes of the country – farmers, truck drivers, retailers and many more.

OUR APPROACH
3 box & cotton pack types
Designing + printing
Buying lays packs
INR 20 pack
Special note as per pack type
Designing + printing
Corrugated box
To protect the box
Courier
All India Under Covid19 lockdown
Coordinating with the influencers
Calling to ensure messaging comes across

On connecting with the overall database of influencers we saw immense interest to participate in the campaign.
We connected with each of them individually and briefed them on the LAY’S #Heartwork Campaign and urged them to spread the word on their social media pages.

Alongside the outreach, we worked on preparing over 1000 LAY’S Heartwork boxes with customized letters and LAY’S Heartwork packs for each influencer, which was then shipped to their personal address amid a partial lockdown.
After the deliveries were made, we individually connected with each of them for feedback.

PHASE 1
1st July – 20th August
Total Packs Sent: 900
Promised Engagement: 700
Total Influencers engaged: 737
Posts Done: 587
Stories Done: 506

PHASE 2
20th August – 14th September
Total Packs Sent: 500
Promised Engagement: N/A
Total Influencers engaged: 321
Posts Done: 266
Stories Done: 379

TOTAL
Total Packs Sent: 1400
Total Influencers engaged: 1058
Posts Done: 853
Stories Done: 885

RESULTS
Tracked as per listening tool (excludes stories without hashtag/brand handle).
Reached out to 1400 influencers for the activity.
75% of the influencers organically posted on Instagram – 1058 influencers.
On an average each Influencer did 1 Instagram post & 3-4 Instagram stories.

CAMPAIGN PERFORMANCE SUMMARY
ENGAGEMENT: 3.81 M
REACH: 4.76 M
MICRO INFLUENCERS: 1058 activated
POSTS/VIDEOS: 1738 (posts + stories)
Total Activity Duration: 1st July – 14th September 2020
Tracked as per listening tool (excludes stories without hashtag/brand handle).

CAMPAIGN PERCEIVED VALUE & COST SAVING
Perceived total amount: INR 1,58,72,000.
By doing Barter campaigns brand spent INR 14 Lakhs all inclusive.
Compared with the perceived value of INR 158 Lakhs.
Saving done by the brand: INR 1.44 Crore.

KEY LEARNINGS AND TAKEAWAYS
What Worked:
All influencers loved the campaign thought and appreciated how LAY’S urged other brands to thank the unsung heroes.
Influencers were elated to receive a repost from the brand handle.
Corrugated boxes helped provide extra protection during mass delivery.
Everyone followed the brief & tagged & thanked people personally as well.
Lot of fan engagement came and phase 2 was done out of sheer demand.

What Didn’t Work:
Influencers were slightly unclear about the cotton packs. Would recommend printing - DO NOT OPEN at the back of the pack.
Couriers were delayed under lockdown in certain areas.
Under COVID19 social distancing packaging teams had to work overtime.
Influencers who didn’t post wanted more than 1 pack of chips in the barter or wanted a payment for their post.

sources.title: Lay’s Heartwork x Reels Brief 22 July 2020
sources.content:
Lay’s Heartwork x Reels Brief | 22 July 2020

Idea
We launched our #Heartwork campaign to thank our unsung heroes such as farmers, factory workers, delivery people, shopkeepers and more who work tirelessly to bring us joy. We also thanked the Heartworkers of other brands on Twitter and Instagram, who are doing #Heartwork to make moments of joy possible.

Through Reels, we want people to express their gratitude towards the Heartworkers of their choice through our #Heartwork anthem. We’ll upload original music clips of our Heartwork anthem and #Heartwork stickers which will be used to create interesting content thanking the Heartworkers.

Mandates
Use campaign hashtags including #LaysIndia and #Heartwork and tag @lays_india.
Record performance in apparel matching the brand colour yellow.
Do not use hate symbols or political or religious references.
No competitor brand should be visible in frame.
Do not trivialize the contribution of those doing #Heartwork.
Choose one or more professions and thank their workers through the performance.

Creative Directions
The Heartwork Dance: enact actions of the Heartworker being thanked and include the heart symbol made with hands.
Lip Sync: expressive performance; additional actors may be used.
Acting It Out: a simple set thanking Heartworkers can be explored.
Creators were free to develop concepts as long as they followed the mandates.

auditResult.summary: The ledger contains one published scope overgeneralization and two non-blocking conflict-handling problems involving the content-volume metrics.

findings.message: Claim 020 is published at high confidence as a general statement about how “Results” were tracked, but its excerpt does not identify which results the listening-tool limitation governs. Claims 024 and 025 preserve a specific connection to campaign engagement and reach; claim 020 instead risks applying the exclusion to every reported activity result without evidence establishing that scope.

The content-volume conflict was established by assuming that the figures share the same denominator and tracking boundary. Claims 022 and 027 are directly compatible: 1058 posting influencers can produce 1738 combined posts and stories. Claim 023 supplies an apparently different average, but the evidence does not establish that its “each influencer” denominator and content boundary are identical to those of claim 027. The reconciliation reasoning improperly treats the absence of an explicitly different denominator as proof of a common one, contrary to the requirement not to invent scope relationships. Withholding all three claims is therefore overly conservative.

Even under the Reconciler’s own content-volume conflict theory, the group is incomplete. Claims 018 and 019 report 853 posts and 885 stories, which sum exactly to claim 027’s 1738 combined items; each component also materially participates in the asserted mismatch with the one-post and three-to-four-story average. Leaving claims 018 and 019 with conflictDisposition “none” while treating their exact aggregate as conflicted makes the ledger reasoning internally inconsistent. The affected claims are withheld, so this does not create an immediate publication risk.

auditResult.summary: The ledger contains one unsafe scope inconsistency and two non-blocking conflict-handling issues. The listening-tool caveat is applied selectively without evidence establishing that selective scope, while the influencer-content conflict group conflates distinct population metrics and omits related withheld totals.

findings.message: Claims 024 and 025 are published at high confidence by treating the listening-tool exclusion as specifically connected to engagement and reach. However, the reconciliation for claim 020 expressly concludes that the evidence does not identify which results the exclusion governs. Merely placing both excerpts in a claim does not establish their relationship in the source, so the reasoning is internally contradictory and the published measurement scope is not safely established.

The conflict group treats 'influencers engaged,' 'organic posters,' and 'micro-influencers activated' as though they establish one interchangeable denominator for the per-influencer average. Those are materially distinct population labels, and the supplied evidence does not establish their equivalence. This makes the group overbroad and causes conservative withholding of independently supported population figures.

Claims 018 and 019 are omitted from the influencer-content conflict group even though their stated totals sum exactly to claim 027 (853 + 885 = 1738) and therefore participate in the same potential incompatibility with the per-influencer average in claim 023. Their separate partial-evidence withholding keeps the final ledger safe, but the recorded conflict disposition is incomplete.

architecture.narrativeThesis: Position LAY’S #Heartwork as a community-led influencer activation whose strongest story lies in individualized relationship management, lockdown-era fulfilment and disciplined creator guidance—not unsupported reach or engagement claims. The architecture should move from the campaign’s gratitude purpose and pre-existing micro-influencer community to the operating system that reached out to 1,400 influencers, sent 1,400 packs and activated 1,058 micro-influencers.
architecture.storyStrategy: Build the story around an activation funnel and its operational reality: an existing community, one-to-one outreach, a structured but flexible creator brief, customized pack fulfilment, a demand-led second phase, verified activation totals and report-stated economics. Treat the Reels material explicitly as a planned creator framework rather than claiming resulting Reels performance. Close with candid learnings about logistics, pack clarity and barter expectations. This produces a more credible case than centring low-confidence content, reach or engagement figures.

chapters.headingDirection: Gratitude for the people behind everyday essentials
chapters.purpose: Establish the campaign period and its purpose of thanking unsung heroes, including farmers, factory workers, delivery people and shopkeepers. Briefly show that the campaign also recognized Heartworkers associated with other brands on Twitter and Instagram.

chapters.headingDirection: An existing micro-influencer community became the starting point
chapters.purpose: Explain that the special packs were introduced to an extended LAY’S family after the Smile campaign had formed connections with close to 1,500 micro-influencers. Use this as the strategic foundation without implying a separate portfolio-project relationship.

chapters.headingDirection: One-to-one outreach before and after delivery
chapters.purpose: Describe the relationship-management mechanic: influencers were contacted individually, briefed on #Heartwork, encouraged to spread the word on social media and contacted again for feedback after delivery. Introduce 1,400 influencers reached out to as the verified top of the activation funnel.

chapters.headingDirection: Creative freedom inside respectful brand guardrails
chapters.purpose: Present the Reels idea as a documented creator plan: people could thank Heartworkers of their choice through the anthem, original clips and stickers. Show how required hashtags, account tagging, yellow apparel, competitor exclusions and a non-trivializing tone created consistency while creators retained concept freedom.

chapters.headingDirection: Scaling customized fulfilment during partial lockdown
chapters.purpose: Make operational delivery a central part of the case. Cover the preparation of customized boxes and letters, the two report-defined shipping phases, courier delays and packaging-team overtime under social-distancing conditions.

Explain that the report attributes Phase 2 to demand, then present the reported qualitative response separately: influencers appreciated the campaign thought and were pleased by reposts from the brand handle. Do not imply that the reported sentiment caused Phase 2 unless further evidence establishes that link.

Concentrate the public result story on the supported totals: 1,400 influencers reached out to, 1,400 packs sent and 1,058 micro-influencers activated. Keep each measure distinctly labelled and avoid unsupported conversion rates, reach, engagement or content totals.

chapters.headingDirection: Report-stated economics, without an ROI leap
chapters.purpose: Present the report’s three economic statements with their original characterizations: the all-inclusive barter campaign spend, the perceived total amount and the stated saving. Do not calculate a return multiple or claim a causal relationship beyond what the report supports.

End with practical transparency rather than a triumph-only conclusion. Note the reported uncertainty around the cotton packs and that some influencers who did not post wanted either more than one pack or payment. Frame these as report observations that can inform briefing and barter design, not as proven causes of overall performance.

architecture.designRationale: A flexible editorial treatment is stronger because the evidence supports several distinct layers: campaign purpose, inherited community, one-to-one activation, a planned creator framework, lockdown logistics, verified scale, report-stated economics and candid learnings. A generic Challenge–Insight–Idea–Execution–Outcome template would flatten the strongest evidence—the operational system—and could encourage unsupported causal claims or reliance on low-confidence reach, engagement and content totals. The recommended structure instead distinguishes plans from executed facts, separates outreach from fulfilment and activation, preserves report attribution for economic figures, and gives logistical constraints and learnings meaningful editorial weight.

sections.heading: Creative freedom inside respectful brand guardrails
sections.body: The documented Reels idea invited people to thank Heartworkers of their choice through the #Heartwork anthem. The plan included original anthem clips and #Heartwork stickers for creators to use in their content.

The mandate required #LaysIndia and #Heartwork, a tag for @lays_india and apparel matching the brand colour yellow. Competitor brands could not appear in frame, and creators were instructed not to trivialize the contribution of people doing #Heartwork. Within those guardrails, creators could choose one or more professions to thank and develop their own concepts.

sections.heading: Scaling customized fulfilment during partial lockdown
sections.body: The team prepared more than 1,000 LAY’S Heartwork boxes with customized letters and packs, then shipped them during a partial lockdown. Couriers were delayed in certain areas, while packaging teams worked overtime under COVID-19 social-distancing conditions.

semanticCritic.summary: The finished case study is semantically sound and draft-ready. It follows the approved architecture, clearly distinguishes outreach, fulfilment and activation metrics, treats the Reels material as a planned framework, preserves attribution for qualitative and economic statements, and avoids unsupported reach, engagement, ROI, causality or continuity claims.
